title: 4 UI Fixes for Real Content
summary: This reel demonstrates how to prevent UI layouts from breaking when faced with real-world data like long names or URLs. It covers four essential CSS fixes: min-width for flexbox, middle truncation, tabular numbers, and overflow wrapping.

transcript.text: This card looks fine until someone signs up with a real name.
Your ellipsis never fires. A flex child refuses to shrink below its own text, so the name shoves the button off the card.
Set min-width to zero on the child that should shrink.
Cutting the end throws away the answer. A file name is its extension, an email is its domain.
Truncate the middle instead and both ends survive.
Live numbers make the row twitch. Proportional digits are different widths, so every update nudges the layout.
Tabular-nums locks them to one width. Dead still.
One long URL can blow out the whole card. Browsers never break inside a word, so the container stretches until your layout gives up.
Overflow-wrap anywhere gives it permission to break.
Follow for more UI systems. Save this before your next demo.
